abstract:
DNA-RNA hybrids (R-loops) form transiently on the genome and regulate cellular homeostasis. They also influence genome editing outcomes, highlighting their therapeutic potential in vivo. This protocol enables high-resolution mapping of DNA-RNA hybrids directly from frozen mouse tissues. Following tissue homogenisation and lysis, genomic DNA is extracted, digested and DNA-RNA hybrids are isolated using the hybrid-specific S9.6 monoclonal antibody. The purified hybrids are then processed for whole-genome sequencing to generate R-loop profiles. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Puzzo, Crossley et al1.
